AAA-001.title: LDAP connection without encryption
AAA-001.rationale: `-secType PLAINTEXT` (also the default when the option is missing) sends the bind DN and passwords in clear text.
AAA-001.remediation: Use `-secType SSL` (LDAPS/636) or `TLS` (StartTLS) and verify the server certificate (`-validateServerCert YES` from 13.1/14.1).

AAA-002.title: LDAPS/TLS without certificate validation
AAA-002.rationale: With `-validateServerCert NO` or no value, the LDAP server certificate is not validated (default depends on the version, hence heuristic).
AAA-002.remediation: Set `-validateServerCert YES` and install the CA on the appliance.

AAA-003.title: Gateway/auth vServer without TLS
AAA-003.rationale: Gateway and authentication vServers must terminate TLS, otherwise credentials cross the network in clear text.
AAA-003.remediation: Use vServer type SSL and bind a certificate.

AAA-004.title: Gateway without authentication
AAA-004.rationale: `-authentication OFF` allows anonymous access; a gateway without a bound auth policy or authn profile offers no login either (assumption: authentication is not handled by other means).
AAA-004.remediation: Bind an auth policy (`bind vpn vserver <gw> -policy <authpol> -priority 100`) or set `-authnProfile`.

AAA-005.title: nFactor: policy label without login schema
AAA-005.rationale: A policy label without `-loginSchema` shows no input fields; it only makes sense with `LSCHEMA_INT` (no UI).
AAA-005.remediation: `add authentication policylabel <name> -loginSchema <schema>`, or deliberately `LSCHEMA_INT` for pass-through factors.

AAA-006.title: nFactor: policy label unreachable
AAA-006.rationale: A policy label that is not reached through any `-nextFactor` is dead configuration.

AAA-007.title: Authentication vServer without policy
AAA-007.rationale: An authentication vServer without a bound policy cannot authenticate anyone.

AAA-008.title: SAML: unsigned assertions accepted
AAA-008.rationale: With `-samlRejectUnsignedAssertion OFF`, unsigned assertions are accepted (impersonation possible).

WAF-001.title: WAF profile without policy binding
WAF-001.rationale: An AppFW profile without a policy protects nothing.
WAF-001.remediation: Create `add appfw policy` and bind it to a vServer or globally.

WAF-002.title: WAF profile without blocking action
WAF-002.rationale: Without `block` in any check action the profile effectively runs in observation mode only. Heuristic: all `...Action` options of the profile are checked; defaults from `-defaults basic/advanced` are not resolved.
WAF-002.remediation: Validate the checks in learning mode, then set `block log stats`.

WAF-003.title: HTTP(S) vServer without WAF
WAF-003.rationale: Overview of HTTP/SSL vServers without an AppFW policy. Whether a WAF is required depends on the protection needs of the application (BSI APP.3.1).
WAF-003.remediation: Bind an AppFW policy where the protection needs require it.

GSLB-001.title: GSLB vServer without domain
GSLB-001.rationale: Without `bind gslb vserver -domainName` the vServer answers no DNS queries.

GSLB-002.title: GSLB without ADNS service
GSLB-002.rationale: GSLB answers require an ADNS service (or DNS proxy operation). Assumption: ADNS is not operated on another appliance.

GSLB-003.title: GSLB vServer with fewer than two services
GSLB-003.rationale: A GSLB vServer with a single service offers no site redundancy.

GSLB-004.title: GSLB metric exchange (MEP) disabled
GSLB-004.rationale: With several sites, no load or status information is exchanged between sites without MEP.

HA-001.title: HA synchronization/propagation disabled
HA-001.rationale: `-haSync DISABLED` or `-haProp DISABLED` leads to configuration drift between the nodes.

HA-002.title: No HA partner configured
HA-002.rationale: A single appliance is a single point of failure (unless cluster/cloud HA is used). Assumption: the partner is not described in this file.
HA-002.remediation: Set up an HA pair or cluster.

REP-001.title: IP reputation rules but feature/settings missing
REP-001.rationale: Policies with `IPREP` expressions are only evaluated if the reputation feature is enabled (assumption: feature name `REP`, may be named differently in 13.1+) and the appliance can fetch reputation data (`set reputation settings`).
REP-001.remediation: Check `enable ns feature REP` and `set reputation settings -proxyServer …` (if a proxy is needed).

MGMT-001.title: Telnet enabled on a NetScaler IP
MGMT-001.rationale: Telnet transmits credentials in clear text.
MGMT-001.remediation: `set ns ip <ip> -telnet DISABLED`; administer via SSH only.

MGMT-002.title: GUI access over unencrypted HTTP
MGMT-002.rationale: `-gui ENABLED` allows the HTTP GUI; `SECUREONLY` enforces HTTPS.
MGMT-002.remediation: `set ns ip <ip> -gui SECUREONLY` (or DISABLED on non-NSIPs).

MGMT-003.title: Management access enabled on SNIP/VIP
MGMT-003.rationale: Management services (SSH/GUI/SNMP) should only be reachable via the NSIP or a management network, not via data-plane addresses.
MGMT-003.remediation: `set ns ip <snip> -mgmtAccess DISABLED -telnet DISABLED -ssh DISABLED -gui DISABLED -snmp DISABLED`; allow management access on the NSIP only, with ACLs where appropriate.

MGMT-004.title: FTP enabled on a NetScaler IP

MGMT-005.title: Strong password policy not enabled
MGMT-005.rationale: Without `-strongpassword ENABLED` and a sufficient minimum length, weak admin passwords are possible.

MGMT-006.title: Password change at first login not enforced

MGMT-007.title: Password in clear text in the configuration
MGMT-007.rationale: A `-password` parameter without `-encrypted`, or a clear-text password in `add system user`, is stored in clear text.
MGMT-007.remediation: Set the password again and `save ns config` so it is stored encrypted; do not hand out clear-text configs.

MGMT-008.title: nsroot password probably never changed
MGMT-008.rationale: A configuration without `set system user nsroot ... -encrypted` suggests the default password (assumption; hashes cannot be checked against 'nsroot' because they are salted).
MGMT-008.remediation: Change the nsroot password; better: personal admin accounts and restrict nsroot.

MGMT-009.title: No external authentication for administrators
MGMT-009.rationale: Without `bind system global <auth-policy>` admins are managed locally only (no central access management or traceability).
MGMT-009.remediation: Create an LDAP/RADIUS/TACACS+ policy for management authentication and bind it with `bind system global`.

MGMT-010.title: No remote logging (syslog/NSLOG)
MGMT-010.rationale: Without a syslog/NSLOG target, audit information is lost on appliance replacement or compromise.
MGMT-010.remediation: `add audit syslogAction ...`, `add audit syslogPolicy ...` and `bind audit syslogGlobal -policyName ...`.

MGMT-011.title: No time synchronization (NTP)
MGMT-011.rationale: Without NTP, logs and certificate validation are unreliable.

MGMT-012.title: SNMP community with default name
MGMT-012.rationale: Default communities (public/private …) are well known; SNMP v1/v2c is unprotected.
MGMT-012.remediation: Change/remove the community, use SNMPv3 (`add snmp user`/`add snmp group`), restrict `add snmp manager` to the monitoring server.

MGMT-013.title: SNMP v1/v2c used instead of SNMPv3
MGMT-013.rationale: Community-based SNMP offers neither encryption nor strong authentication.

MGMT-014.title: HTTP hardening parameters not set
MGMT-014.rationale: The Secure Deployment Guide recommends, among others, `set ns httpParam -dropInvalReqs ON` (drop invalid HTTP requests). Please verify the exact recommendation against the current version of the guide.

QA-001.title: LB vServer without bound service
QA-001.rationale: An LB vServer without a service/service group has no backend and is DOWN.
QA-001.remediation: Bind a service/service group or remove the vServer.

QA-002.title: Service/service group not bound to any vServer
QA-002.rationale: Unbound services cause monitoring load and confusion without benefit.

QA-004.title: Policy without binding
QA-004.rationale: A policy that is bound nowhere has no effect.

QA-005.title: Unused certificate
QA-005.rationale: Unused certificates increase the attack surface and obscure expiry monitoring.

QA-007.title: Reference to non-existent object
QA-007.rationale: A binding/option refers to an object that does not exist in the configuration (typo, incomplete export or deleted object). With partial exports this is expected — assumption: the config is complete.
QA-007.remediation: Create the object or correct the reference.

QA-008.title: Duplicate vServer address (IP:port)
QA-008.rationale: Two vServers with the same IP/port/protocol collide.

QA-009.title: Objects configured but feature not enabled
QA-009.rationale: Without `enable ns feature <X>` the objects of that function are ineffective (and sometimes cannot be created).

QA-010.title: CS vServer without target
QA-010.rationale: A CS vServer without a default LB vServer and without policies does nothing useful.
QA-010.remediation: Bind a default LB vServer (`bind cs vserver <cs> <lb>`) and/or CS policies.

QA-011.title: HTTPS vServer without HTTP→HTTPS redirect
QA-011.rationale: Users who type http:// cannot reach the service. (Heuristic: `-redirectFromPort` and a vServer on port 80 on the same IP are checked.)
QA-011.remediation: `-redirectFromPort 80 -httpsRedirectUrl https://<fqdn>` or a redirect vServer on port 80.

QA-012.title: vServer administratively disabled
QA-012.rationale: Disabled vServers often remain in configs as legacy.

TLS-001.title: SSLv3 enabled
TLS-001.rationale: SSLv3 is broken by POODLE and not permitted by TR-02102-2.
TLS-001.remediation: `set ssl vserver <vs> -ssl3 DISABLED` or in the SSL profile.

TLS-002.title: TLS 1.0/1.1 enabled
TLS-002.rationale: TLS 1.0 and 1.1 are considered obsolete; TR-02102-2 recommends TLS 1.2/1.3.
TLS-002.remediation: `-tls1 DISABLED -tls11 DISABLED` on the vServer or SSL profile.

TLS-003.title: Weak ciphers bound
TLS-003.rationale: RC4, (3)DES, EXPORT, NULL, MD5 and anonymous suites are not permitted by TR-02102-2; the group ALL contains such suites.
TLS-003.remediation: Bind your own cipher group with ECDHE AEAD suites (TLS 1.3 + TLS 1.2 GCM); `unbind ssl vserver <vs> -cipherName DEFAULT/ALL`.

TLS-004.title: TLS 1.2 disabled
TLS-004.rationale: Without TLS 1.2 only obsolete protocols remain (or TLS 1.3 only).

TLS-005.title: TLS 1.3 not enabled
TLS-005.rationale: TLS 1.3 is supported since NetScaler 12.1 and recommended by TR-02102-2. Only explicitly disabled TLS 1.3 is reported; missing values (defaults depend on version/profile) are an assumption.

TLS-007.title: Self-signed default certificate on vServer
TLS-007.rationale: `ns-server-certificate` is self-signed and device-specific; clients cannot validate it.
TLS-007.remediation: Bind a certificate from a trusted CA.

TLS-008.title: SSL vServer without certificate
TLS-008.rationale: A TLS-terminating vServer without a bound certificate is DOWN or cannot complete handshakes.

TLS-009.title: Certificate expiry monitoring disabled
TLS-009.rationale: With `-expiryMonitor DISABLED` there is no warning before expiry. The actual expiry date is not in the ns.conf and cannot be checked here.

TLS-010.title: Backend TLS without certificate validation
TLS-010.rationale: SSL services without `-serverAuth ENABLED` (or a backend profile with serverAuth) do not validate the server certificate; man-in-the-middle in the backend network goes unnoticed. The result is heuristic because profiles/defaults vary by version.
TLS-010.remediation: Bind an SSL backend profile with `-serverAuth ENABLED` and a CA certificate to the service (group).

TLS-011.title: No HSTS configured
TLS-011.rationale: Without an HTTP Strict Transport Security header, browsers can fall back to HTTP.
TLS-011.remediation: Rewrite policy with `Strict-Transport-Security`, or `-HSTS ENABLED` in the SSL profile.

HA-003.title: Configuration drift between HA nodes
HA-003.rationale: After synchronization both nodes should be identical (except node-specific objects such as NSIP, hostname, interfaces). Drift leads to different behavior after failover.
HA-003.remediation: Check sync (`show ha node`, `force ha sync`), clarify causes (manual change with -haProp DISABLED, sync errors).

CHAIN-001.title: Double hop: match by IP only
CHAIN-001.rationale: The backend target matches a frontend address of the downstream NetScaler only in the IP, not in the port (e.g. port mapping/NAT in between). The match is an assumption.

CHAIN-002.title: Double hop: connection between the NetScalers unencrypted
CHAIN-002.rationale: The frontend NetScaler talks to the backend NetScaler via HTTP/TCP although a network worth protecting may lie in between (e.g. DMZ → internal).
CHAIN-002.remediation: Use service type SSL with server certificate validation (backend profile).
